_about: Every statement the app makes about the Claude app, Claude Code and where a chat runs: what each surface can do, how to reach it, and how a cloud task is made from a computer. Messages read their words from here (tools/claude_surfaces.py say), docs carry them in marked blocks (sync-docs), and tests/test_claude_surfaces.py fails on a statement outside it. Each entry is dated and sourced; `watch` (the maintainer's, run by .github/workflows/claude-surfaces-watch.yml in the app only) checks each quote is still on its page and flags entries after a new Claude Code release. A path a person follows is written as a destination or as numbered steps and never tells them to press, click, tap or find anything; the day it was checked and its official page are for Claude (`source`), never the person.

entries.claim: A cloud chat that another started with create_session can send that chat a message with send_message: it arrives there as a new turn, marked as sent by the other chat and not typed by the person. So a job's chat reports back once its work is landed, and the chat that started it puts the results on the page and archives it with archive_session, which takes it off the sidebar's list (kept, and it can be brought back). An archived chat cannot accept new messages, so the job's chat sends before it is archived, and a message to a chat archived meanwhile (a helper replaced by a fresh one) is refused: then the job's chat brings the page up to date itself. code.claude.com documents a project's threads reporting back to their conversation, not a chat started this way: the app rests on the tool's own description and on a run seen to do it.

entries.claim: Once the computer lets claude.ai start sessions on it, list_environments shows it as an environment of kind bridge, state active, named after the computer and the shared folder, with the description Bridge environment (<computer>). A cloud chat starts a chat there with create_session and that environment_id. The first such call from a chat is refused until the person approves one card (confirm_repository_trust), and that approval ties the asking chat to their trusted devices for good, so it is asked from a chat no scheduled task fires into. The chat it starts runs in the shared folder (the folder, not a copy inside it, so it looks for the copy there), keeps the computer's own tools, the Browser pane among them, and takes the permission_mode it is given, never more than the asking chat's own. The docs are silent on bridge environments: when one appears, whether pinning a folder changes where its chats start, and Windows.

entries.claim: A cloud chat can ask to work in a folder the computer shares (list_computer_folders, then request_computer_folder), but only where that computer offers it to cloud chats. A folder listed under cannot_be_used with the reason not_available is in the person's list but not offered, and the tool says using a folder from a cloud chat is not available to everyone yet. So it is tried only when a folder is listed as usable, and never relied on. Which computers can serve one depends on the app's version there: on Windows not every version can (the tool's own words), and a folder listed under cannot_be_used comes with its explanation, which is what the person is told. The tool also says not to send anyone to claude remote-control to add a folder, which for most accounts offers a cloud chat nothing.

entries.claim: A chat in the desktop app can list the app's other chats on that computer and archive them, asked in plain words: the docs name no tool for it. It sees only the chats the desktop app runs itself (local, SSH and WSL ones in the Code tab), the 20 most recently active by default, never archived ones unless asked, and never the chat it is in; it does not see cloud chats. Whether a chat the cloud started on the computer has this too is not documented: the one on a Mac on 2026-11-10 listed the others and found none to archive, because the person had deleted the earlier chat by hand, and that chat (the setup one, named by the desktop app from the line pasted into it) did not carry the app's name either. Archiving it in the desktop app archives its copy on the person's other devices too, but the docs do not say the reverse: a chat on the computer archived from the cloud (archive_session) was seen still listed in the desktop app. So each chat the app starts on the computer archives the app's earlier finished ones there (computer.py archivable picks them by name), and where it cannot list them it says nothing.

entries.claim: A scheduled task made by a chat (create_trigger) either fires into one chat it is bound to (persistent_session_id) or starts a fresh chat each run. A fresh chat a run has no copy of the person's files attached, no add_repo and no way to clone one, so the brief cannot run there. A chat that approves computer access (confirm_repository_trust) is limited to the person's own trusted devices for good, and a scheduled task bound to it then fails, so the brief runs in a chat of its own, made with create_session and the person's copy as its source_url, and no chat that may approve computer access sets a reminder (send_later) for itself. A manual fire_trigger of a task bound to a chat starts a fresh chat instead, so a manual test cannot show the bound run: a one-off task bound to the same chat a few minutes on does.
